nodes.title: Board as flat Uint8Array with hidden buffer rows

nodes.title: Render with a single canvas

nodes.title: Render: single canvas redrawn every frame

nodes.title: Render with Canvas 2D

nodes.title: Render: DOM grid of 200 divs with CSS classes

nodes.title: Board as array of row arrays

nodes.title: Render: 200 DOM cells, toggle classes

nodes.title: Board: flat Uint8Array, 10x40 with hidden rows above

nodes.title: Board as array of row arrays, 0 = empty, else piece id
nodes.description: grid[row][col], 10 wide, 20 visible rows plus 2 hidden spawn rows above. Line clear is filter-out-full-rows then unshift empty rows: no index math. Cell holds the tetromino letter so colour comes from the piece table.

nodes.title: Board: array of row arrays, 0 = empty, else piece index

nodes.title: SRS rotation: 4 explicit orientations per piece + kick tables
nodes.description: Store each piece as 4 precomputed orientation cell lists (derived once at load from the spawn shape by rotating within its bounding box, 3x3 or 4x4). nodes.title: Rotation: SRS with full wall kick tables

Players expect T-spins and I-piece kicks to behave like modern Tetris. Cost: the tables must be exactly right; a typo is invisible until a kick fails.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with standard kick tables
nodes.description: Pieces defined as 4 explicit rotation states each (cell offset lists), plus the two SRS kick tables (JLSTZ and I). O never kicks. This is what modern guideline Tetris does and it is what players expect for T-spins and wall kicks.

nodes.title: Board as flat Uint8Array with hidden buffer rows

nodes.title: Board: array of row arrays
nodes.description: board[y][x], rows are JS arrays. Line clear is splice + unshift. Readable but allocates per clear and every cell access is two lookups. Negative y for spawn needs a guard.

nodes.title: Board: array of row arrays, 0 = empty, N = piece colour id
nodes.description: board[y][x]. Line clear is filter-out-full-rows then unshift empty rows until height is restored. Reads naturally in the code the others will look at. Includes hidden rows above the visible top so pieces can spawn and rotate partially off-screen.

nodes.title: Board as flat Uint8Array with index math
nodes.description: 200-entry typed array, idx = row*10+col. Fastest, but line clears become copyWithin calls and every reader repeats the index math. Speed is irrelevant at 10x22.

nodes.title: Rendering: DOM grid of 200 cells with CSS classes
nodes.description: 200 divs in a CSS grid, colour by class. Easy to style, inspectable in devtools, but every frame diffs classes across 200 nodes and a ghost piece means another layer of cells. Fine for Tetris speed, more code per feature.

nodes.title: Matrix-transpose rotation, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the piece matrix in place, reject if it collides. Simplest possible. Feels bad against walls: rotation near a wall just fails, and I piece rotation is off-centre.

nodes.title: Matrix-transpose rotation, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the NxN matrix in place. Less code, but the I piece and rotation pivots come out wrong compared to SRS and rotating next to a wall simply fails.

nodes.title: Loop: requestAnimationFrame with delta-time accumulator for gravity and lock delay
nodes.description: Single rAF loop; each frame adds dt to a gravity accumulator and, when the piece is grounded, a lock-delay timer. Rendering every frame keeps ghost and DAS smooth; timers stay in ms so level speed is a lookup, not an interval reset. Tab-hidden frames get clamped so the piece does not teleport.

nodes.title: Board as array of row arrays
nodes.description: board[y][x], the textbook form. Line clear is splice + unshift. Readable, slightly more allocation, no hidden rows unless added explicitly.

nodes.title: Board: one Uint16 bitmask per row
nodes.description: Row as a 10-bit mask; collision is a single AND, full row is mask == 0x3FF. Fast, but colours need a parallel array and every collision needs the piece rendered as row masks per rotation. Speed is not the bottleneck for a 10x20 board at 60fps.

nodes.title: Board: flat Uint8Array with y*W+x indexing
nodes.description: Faster and compact but line clearing needs copyWithin arithmetic and every reader has to do index math in their head. Not worth it for a 10x22 grid.

nodes.title: Rotation: matrix transpose+reverse, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the shape matrix in place, reject if it collides. Ten lines of code. But the I and O pieces wobble around their box, rotation near walls simply fails, and there is no path to T-spins. Good enough for milestone 2, a dead end for milestone 4.

nodes.title: Loop: setInterval per level, re-armed on level change
nodes.description: clearInterval/setInterval when the level changes. Easy, but input handling and lock delay then need their own timers, and rendering only on tick makes movement feel laggy.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with the standard wall-kick tables
nodes.description: Super Rotation System: each piece has 4 explicit rotation states as cell offsets; rotating tries the base position then up to 4 kick offsets from the JLSTZ table or the I table. This is what modern guideline Tetris does and enables T-spins. The tables are small and well-known; the cost is getting the I-piece table right.

nodes.title: requestAnimationFrame loop with ms accumulator
nodes.description: One rAF loop. Gravity, lock delay, DAS and ARR are all timers in ms advanced by the frame delta, so speed is independent of frame rate and pausing is just not advancing the clock.

nodes.title: Board: array of row arrays, 0 = empty, 1..7 = piece id
nodes.description: grid[row][col]. Line clear is filter-out-full-rows then unshift fresh rows, which is the simplest correct implementation. Two hidden buffer rows above the visible 20 so pieces spawn out of view and top-out is detected by overlap at spawn.

nodes.title: Rotation: SRS with explicit kick tables
nodes.description: Store each tetromino as four precomputed orientations of [dx,dy] cell offsets inside a 3x3 (I and O: 4x4) box, matching the Super Rotation System. Kicks come from the standard SRS offset tables (one for JLSTZ, one for I, O never kicks). This gives T-spins, I-piece wall kicks and the behaviour players expect from Guideline games. More data up front, but rotation becomes a pure table lookup plus five collision tests.

nodes.title: requestAnimationFrame loop with dt accumulator
nodes.description: One rAF loop. Gravity is a timer in ms (dropInterval per level) advanced by the frame delta; DAS/ARR for horizontal auto-repeat and lock delay are also ms timers advanced by the same dt. Render every frame. Tab-hidden frames are clamped so a returned tab does not fast-forward 30 seconds of gravity.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with guideline kick tables
nodes.description: Store each tetromino as 4 pre-rotated cell lists (states 0..3) rather than rotating matrices at runtime. Kicks from the SRS tables: one table for JLSTZ, one for I, O never kicks. 7-bag randomizer. This is what players expect from modern Tetris and makes T-spins possible.

nodes.title: Rotation: SRS with guideline kick tables
nodes.description: Each piece has 4 explicit rotation states as 4x4 (I) or 3x3 matrices; kicks are the standard JLSTZ table and the separate I table, indexed by (from,to). This is what players expect (T-spins, I-kicks) and milestone 4's wall kicks become a table lookup instead of a rewrite.

nodes.title: Rotation: SRS with the standard kick tables
nodes.description: Super Rotation System: pieces stored as 4 explicit rotation states in a 3x3 (I: 4x4) box, plus the JLSTZ and I kick tables (5 tests per transition). This is what modern players expect: T-spins, wall kicks off both sides, I kicks through gaps. The kick table is data, so it is 20 lines.

nodes.title: Loop: requestAnimationFrame with time accumulator
nodes.description: One rAF loop; gravity is a millisecond budget per row that shrinks per level, accumulated from frame deltas. Input handled on keydown with DAS/ARR timers driven by the same clock. Pauses cleanly by not accumulating. Alternative setInterval per gravity tick drifts and fights with soft drop / lock delay.

nodes.title: setInterval per level
nodes.description: Reset the interval whenever the level changes. Simple but soft drop, lock delay and key repeat each need their own timers and they drift relative to each other.

nodes.title: Matrix-transpose rotation, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the piece's NxN matrix in place; fail if it collides. Ten lines of code, but the I and O pieces wobble and rotation next to a wall just fails, which feels bad.

nodes.title: setInterval gravity tick, render on change
nodes.description: setInterval(step, dropInterval), reset the interval when level changes. Simple, but input auto-repeat and lock delay then need their own timers, and drift between timers makes feel inconsistent.

nodes.title: Board: flat Uint8Array indexed row*W+col
nodes.description: Cache friendly and trivially copyable, but line clear becomes copyWithin arithmetic and every access needs the index math. Speed is irrelevant at 10x22 cells; the readability cost is not worth it.

nodes.title: Rotation: matrix transpose+reverse, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the piece matrix at runtime (transpose then reverse rows). Small code, but I and O drift on rotation in an even-sized box, there is no standard kick behaviour, and wall kicks become ad-hoc nudges. Fine for milestone 2, wrong for milestone 4.

nodes.title: Matrix rotation, no kicks (NES style)
nodes.description: Rotate the shape matrix 90 degrees at runtime; if it collides, refuse. Simplest to write, but rotating against a wall silently fails, which feels bad to anyone who has played a modern Tetris.

nodes.title: Rotation: matrix transpose+reverse with nudge kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the shape matrix mathematically and try offsets 0, +1, -1, +2, -2 horizontally. Less code, but the I and O pieces wobble around their box centre and there are no proper T-spin or floor kicks.

nodes.title: Rotation: matrix transpose+reverse, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the shape matrix in place. Simple, but the I and O pieces wobble around their box, and adding kicks later means bolting a table onto a system that has no notion of rotation state index.

nodes.title: Loop: setInterval gravity tick
nodes.description: setInterval(step, speed) and clearInterval/reset on level change. Simple, but timers drift, soft drop needs a second timer, and lock delay needs a third. Rendering separately from stepping doubles the bookkeeping.

nodes.title: requestAnimationFrame loop with delta-time accumulators
nodes.description: One rAF loop. Each frame adds elapsed ms to a gravity accumulator and to the DAS/ARR input timers; when the gravity accumulator exceeds the level interval the piece drops. Rendering happens every frame regardless. Pause just stops accumulating. Tab-away is handled by clamping dt.

nodes.title: Rotation: SRS with standard wall-kick tables
nodes.description: Four rotation states per piece derived from the guideline spawn shape by rotating the matrix, plus the JLSTZ and I kick tables keyed by (from,to). This is what modern players expect: T-spins work, I rotates in tight wells, pieces rotate against walls instead of refusing.

nodes.title: Loop: requestAnimationFrame with accumulated gravity timer
nodes.description: One rAF loop. Each frame adds dt to a gravity accumulator; when it exceeds the level's drop interval the piece steps down. Input is handled on keydown with DAS/ARR timers ticked in the same loop, so held keys auto-repeat at a fixed rate independent of the OS key repeat. Lock delay is another accumulator reset on successful move. Render every frame. Pausing simply stops ticking accumulators.

nodes.title: rAF loop with gravity accumulator and DAS/ARR input
nodes.description: requestAnimationFrame drives everything. Gravity is a ms accumulator per level (guideline curve: (0.8 - (level-1)*0.007)^(level-1) seconds per row). Held left/right repeats via DAS (delay) then ARR (rate) measured in ms, not frames, so it feels the same at 60 and 120Hz. Lock delay 500ms with move reset, capped at 15 resets.

nodes.title: Loop: requestAnimationFrame + gravity accumulator + lock delay
nodes.description: rAF gives timestamps; accumulate elapsed ms and step gravity every level's interval. Lock delay (500ms, reset on successful move/rotate, capped at 15 resets) runs on the same clock. Input DAS/ARR also timed off the same clock so feel is consistent across frame rates.

nodes.title: Loop: requestAnimationFrame with a millisecond gravity accumulator
nodes.description: One rAF loop. Each frame adds dt to a gravity accumulator; when it exceeds the level's drop interval, the piece steps down. Lock delay and DAS/ARR run on the same clock. Rendering happens every frame regardless. dt is clamped so a background tab does not dump 30 seconds of gravity on return.

nodes.title: Canvas rendering, full redraw per frame
nodes.description: Chose canvas over DOM. A 10x22 grid redrawn from a Uint8Array is under 300 fillRect calls per frame, trivially cheap, and overlays (ghost, active piece, clear flash) are just more draw calls in order rather than DOM state to reconcile. Cost: no CSS styling of cells, so colours live in JS.

nodes.title: setInterval gravity timer, redraw on change
nodes.description: A setInterval fires the drop; level changes clear and reset the interval. Simple, but auto-repeat input needs its own timers, and mixing several timers makes pause and level changes fiddly.

nodes.title: Rotation: matrix rotate, reject on collision, no kicks
nodes.description: Rotate the shape matrix in place and refuse if it overlaps. Ten lines of code, but rotation next to a wall silently fails, which feels broken to anyone who has played a modern Tetris. Milestone 4 explicitly asks for wall kicks so this would be rewritten anyway.

nodes.title: setInterval tick loop
nodes.description: setInterval(tick, msPerRow) re-armed on each level change. Simple but input repeat and lock delay then live on separate timers, and the tab-hidden behaviour drifts.

nodes.title: Loop: setInterval per level speed
nodes.description: setInterval(step, speed), clearInterval and restart on level change. Simple but drifts, fights with pause, and input repeat is left to the OS keydown repeat which varies by machine and has a long initial delay.

nodes.title: Loop: setInterval reset on each level change
nodes.description: setInterval(step, dropMs), cleared and recreated when the level changes. Simple, but input timing (DAS, lock delay) needs its own timers and the render is coupled to the gravity tick.

nodes.title: Loop: setInterval per gravity tick, re-created on level up
nodes.description: Simplest possible loop. But the interval has to be torn down and rebuilt on every speed change, pause, and restart, and rendering is coupled to gravity ticks so soft drop and DAS need their own timers. Drifts under tab throttling.

nodes.title: Flat Uint8Array board, 10 wide, 20 visible + 2 buffer rows
nodes.description: Chose flat typed array over row arrays. Collision is one loop over 4 cells with y*W+x indexing, no nested arrays to copy. Two hidden buffer rows let pieces spawn above the visible field, which gives the correct top-out rule: game over when a piece locks fully inside the buffer or the spawn position is blocked. Line clear shifts everything above down with copyWithin.

nodes.title: Loop: requestAnimationFrame with a gravity accumulator
nodes.description: One rAF loop. Each frame adds dt to a gravity accumulator and steps the piece down while it exceeds the per-level interval. Lock delay, DAS/ARR and clear animation are all timers in the same tick, so pause is one flag. Rendering happens once per frame regardless of speed.

nodes.title: Files: classic script tags, one file per concern, shared global scope
nodes.description: pieces.js, board.js, game.js, render.js, input.js, main.js loaded in order. Not ES modules: Chrome blocks module imports from file:// so index.html would not open by double-click. Top-level const in classic scripts is shared across files, which is enough namespacing for six files.

nodes.title: Canvas rendering, full redraw per frame
nodes.description: Chose canvas over a DOM grid. The board is tiny (220 cells) so a full redraw is free, and every later feature (ghost piece, line-clear flash, hold/preview boxes) is just more rects on the same surface. A DOM grid would make ghost rendering and flashes need extra elements or class juggling.

nodes.title: Canvas 2D rendering, full redraw per frame
nodes.description: Chosen over a DOM grid because the board is small (10x20) and redrawing 200 cells on a canvas each frame costs nothing, while ghost piece, lock flash and line-clear animation are just extra fillRect calls instead of class plumbing. Scale by devicePixelRatio so cells are crisp on retina.

nodes.title: Loop: setInterval per gravity tick, re-armed on level change
nodes.description: Simplest to write for milestone 1 but every timed feature (lock delay, DAS, clear flash) needs its own timer, and level changes need clearInterval/setInterval. Input handlers render out of band, so frames are inconsistent.

nodes.title: Canvas rendering, HUD in plain DOM
nodes.description: Board, ghost, hold box and next queue are drawn on canvases; score/level/lines and the overlays (paused, game over) are ordinary HTML so they can be styled and read. One draw() per frame from state. Chosen because everything visual reduces to coloured squares and canvas makes that one function.

nodes.title: SRS with explicit rotation states and kick tables
nodes.description: Chose SRS. Each tetromino is a list of 4 rotation states, each a list of 4 [x,y] cells in a 3x3 (or 4x4 for I) box, matching the guideline diagrams exactly. Rotation tries the 5 kick offsets from the JLSTZ or I table for the (from,to) pair and takes the first that fits. This costs a ~40 line table but wall kicks and T-spins then behave the way anyone who has played modern Tetris expects. Doing it now, not in milestone 4, because retrofitting rotation states is worse than writing them once.

nodes.title: Board is board[y][x] of piece indices with 2 hidden rows on top
nodes.description: Chose row arrays over bitmasks. Readability wins: collision is a nested loop anyone can audit, line clear is filter + unshift, and the cell value is the colour index so render needs no lookup. Two hidden rows above the visible 20 let pieces spawn partly off-screen, which is how SRS spawn works and avoids instant top-outs on a full-looking board.

nodes.title: Flat Uint8Array board, 10x22 with 2 hidden rows
nodes.description: Chosen over row arrays because collision becomes a single index lookup with no nested bounds checks, line clears are copyWithin on a typed array, and the hidden rows give a guideline-correct spawn above the visible field so game-over is 'spawn overlaps' rather than 'top row filled'. Cell value 0 = empty, 1..7 = tetromino id, which also picks the color.

nodes.title: Render with canvas 2D, full redraw per frame
nodes.description: Chosen over a DOM grid. Ghost piece, lock flash and line-clear animation are all just extra fillRect calls on the same frame. Cell size is a single constant so the board scales with CSS. Nobody else had logged a rendering decision yet when this was made.

nodes.title: Canvas rendering, full redraw each frame
nodes.description: Chose canvas over DOM cells. The board is small enough that redrawing everything per frame costs nothing, and it removes the entire class of "DOM out of sync with state" bugs. Ghost piece and line-clear flash become pure draw code.

nodes.title: Single rAF loop; gravity, lock delay, DAS/ARR are ms timers
nodes.description: Chose rAF + delta time. One clock drives everything: gravity interval per level, a 500 ms lock delay with move-reset (capped at 15 resets so you cannot stall forever), and DAS 170 ms / ARR 40 ms for held left/right. Pause stops the clock; nothing else needs to know. Frame-rate independent, and a 144 Hz monitor plays the same as 60.

nodes.title: Board is 22 rows of 10, rows are arrays, cells hold the piece letter
nodes.description: grid[r][c] with 2 hidden rows on top for spawn. Line clear = grid.filter(row => row.some(c => !c)) then pad the top. Cells hold 'I','O','T'... or 0, so render looks up colour by letter and there is no separate colour grid. Chosen over a typed array because clarity beats speed at 220 cells.

nodes.title: Render on a single canvas
nodes.description: Chose canvas over a DOM grid. Every feature after milestone 1 (ghost piece, clear flash, lock-delay hint) is a draw call on canvas but a second layer of nodes in the DOM. Board is drawn from state every frame so there is no sync bug class at all.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with the standard JLSTZ and I kick tables
nodes.description: Chose SRS. Rotation states are stored as explicit cell offsets per state, not computed, so there is no ambiguity about pivot points. The kick table is the one from the Tetris Guideline: 5 tests per transition, separate table for I, O never kicks. This gives real wall kicks, floor kicks and T-spins for the cost of two small data tables.

nodes.title: SRS with pre-rotated states, kick tables, 7-bag
nodes.description: Chosen over runtime matrix rotation because pre-rotated cell lists make the rotation index the single source of truth for which kick table row applies, and SRS kicks are what make rotating against a wall feel right. The cost is a data table of 7 pieces x 4 states, which is ~30 lines. 7-bag keeps droughts bounded.

nodes.title: Board is a flat Uint8Array with 2 hidden rows above the visible 20
nodes.description: Chosen over nested row arrays. Hidden rows let pieces spawn above the skyline and make top-out detection precise: game over is spawn collision, not 'a cell in row 0'. Line clear shifts rows with copyWithin. Cell value is the piece id so the renderer needs no separate color grid.

nodes.title: Board is rows of colour ids, 10 wide x 22 tall (2 hidden)
nodes.description: board[y][x], 0 empty, 1..7 piece id used as colour index. Two hidden rows above the visible 20 so spawn and top-of-well rotations work. Line clear = filter full rows + unshift blanks. Readable over fast.

nodes.title: Board is an array of rows with 2 hidden buffer rows
nodes.description: grid[row][col] of small ints, 22 rows of which the top 2 are hidden. Line clear is filter + unshift. Spawn happens in the buffer so top-out is 'spawned piece overlaps' rather than a special case. Rejected the flat typed array: readability wins at this size.

nodes.title: SRS: pieces as 4 explicit rotation states plus kick tables
nodes.description: Each tetromino is stored as 4 arrays of [dx,dy] cell offsets (one per rotation state), generated once at load from the guideline 3x3/4x4 matrices rather than hand-typed. Rotation = pick next state, try the 5 kick offsets from the JLSTZ or I table in order, first non-colliding wins. O never kicks. Chosen so wall kicks and T-spins come for free at milestone 4 without rewriting rotation.

nodes.title: Canvas 2D rendering, whole-board redraw per frame
nodes.description: Chose canvas over DOM. 220 cells redrawn per frame is nothing for canvas, and ghost piece, line-clear flash and lock-delay visual all become a fillRect with alpha instead of extra CSS classes. Scale the canvas by devicePixelRatio so cells are crisp on retina. One draw function reads the board, active piece and ghost; nothing else touches pixels.

nodes.title: rAF loop with dt accumulators for gravity, lock delay and DAS
nodes.description: Chose requestAnimationFrame + delta time. One clock drives gravity, lock delay and auto-repeat, so speeding up a level is changing one number. dt is clamped to 100ms so returning to a background tab does not slam the piece to the floor. Rendering is decoupled from the gravity tick, which is what makes soft-drop and DAS feel smooth.

nodes.title: Single rAF loop, ms-based gravity, DAS/ARR, lock delay
nodes.description: Chosen over setInterval because one clock in ms lets gravity, key repeat and lock delay all be accumulators over the same dt, which stays correct across refresh rates and after a tab is hidden (dt is clamped). Guideline gravity curve so levels feel like a real Tetris rather than an arbitrary ramp.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with standard kick tables from milestone 2 onward
nodes.description: Chosen over runtime matrix rotation with nudge kicks. Doing SRS from the start means milestone 4 wall kicks are free and the I piece rotates around the right center. Shapes are stored as 4 explicit orientations per piece so rotation is an index change, never a matrix op at runtime.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with explicit 4-state tables per piece
nodes.description: Rotation state is an index 0..3 into a precomputed list of cell offsets per piece. Wall kicks (milestone 4) index the standard SRS kick tables by (from, to). Chosen because it is what players expect and because it makes kicks a data change, not a code change.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with wall kicks from the start
nodes.description: Build rotation as (piece, state, kickTable) from milestone 2 rather than bolting kicks on at 4. Rotation states are precomputed by rotating the spawn matrix, so shapes are data and the kick table is the only hand-typed table. Rejected no-kick rotation: it would be thrown away at milestone 4.

nodes.title: Canvas 2D rendering, DPR-aware, redraw whole board each frame
nodes.description: Chosen over a DOM grid because ghost piece, lock flash, and line-clear animation are all trivial when the frame is drawn from the model each tick. Board and preview/hold panels each get their own canvas. Canvas scaled by devicePixelRatio so cells stay crisp on retina.

nodes.title: Single rAF loop; gravity, lock delay and DAS are ms accumulators
nodes.description: update(dt) advances gravity, lock delay and horizontal auto-repeat from one clock. dt is clamped to 100ms so a background tab does not dump a second of gravity on return. Level speed is a lookup into a ms-per-row table. Pause is a flag that skips update() but still draws. Chosen because one clock means one place to pause and one place to reason about timing.

nodes.title: rAF loop with a single ms clock for gravity, lock delay and DAS
nodes.description: One requestAnimationFrame loop; every timed behaviour (gravity per level, 500ms lock delay with capped resets, DAS/ARR autorepeat) accumulates elapsed ms from the same timestamp. Pause just stops advancing the clock. No intervals to tear down.

nodes.title: Flat Uint8Array board, 10x22 with 2 hidden rows
nodes.description: Chose flat typed array over row arrays. Collision test is a 4-iteration loop with one index computation; no nested arrays to allocate or copy. Line clear uses copyWithin to shift rows down in one call. The two hidden rows above the visible field let pieces spawn at y=0..1 partially out of view, so game over is exactly 'the spawn position collides', with no special-casing.

nodes.title: rAF loop with ms accumulators for gravity, lock delay, DAS/ARR
nodes.description: Chosen over setInterval. All timing is in milliseconds against a dt that is clamped to 100ms so a backgrounded tab does not hard-drop the piece on return. Gravity per level is a table lookup (guideline curve), lock delay 500ms with move reset capped at 15, DAS 170ms / ARR 40ms handled in the same loop from a held-keys set.

nodes.title: One rAF loop, all timers as accumulated milliseconds
nodes.description: Gravity, lock delay, DAS/ARR and the line-clear flash are all 'ms remaining' fields ticked by the same dt. Pause freezes the tick. Rejected setInterval: one timer per feature and a re-arm on every level change.

nodes.title: Flat Uint8Array board, 10x22 with 2 hidden spawn rows
nodes.description: Chosen over nested arrays: collision is one index calc, line clears are copyWithin with zero allocation, and hidden rows above the visible field let pieces spawn at guideline row 21/22 and rotate before entering view. Game over = spawn collides (block out). Render only rows >= HIDDEN.

nodes.title: Six classic scripts, no modules, so file:// double-click works
nodes.description: pieces.js (data), board.js (grid + collision + clears), game.js (state machine, scoring, spawn/lock), render.js (canvas), input.js (keys, DAS), main.js (loop). ES modules would be cleaner but Chrome refuses module imports over file://, and the brief says index.html must open in a browser.

nodes.title: SRS with precomputed orientations and standard kick tables
nodes.description: Chose SRS. Shapes are defined once as strings in their spawn orientation inside a 3x3 (or 4x4 for I) box; the other three orientations are derived at load by rotating the box, so the data stays readable and the offsets match guideline SRS exactly. Kicks are the standard JLSTZ and I tables indexed by (from, to). Rotation attempts each of the 5 kicks in order and takes the first non-colliding one. 180 rotation is not in scope.

nodes.title: Render with canvas 2D, DPR-scaled
nodes.description: Canvas over DOM. The board is 200 cells redrawn every frame from the Uint8Array; that is ~200 fillRect calls, trivial. Ghost piece, line-clear flash and the hidden-row spawn area are all just draw calls with no layout consequences. Scale the backing store by devicePixelRatio so cell edges are crisp on retina. Next and hold get their own small canvases so the board draw stays a single function of (board, piece).

nodes.title: SRS rotation with guideline kick tables from milestone 2
nodes.description: Chosen over matrix rotation because wall kicks are a milestone 4 target and retrofitting kicks onto ad-hoc rotation means rewriting piece data. Pieces are defined as 4 pre-baked rotation states (lists of [x,y] cells), kicks are the standard JLSTZ and I tables indexed by (from,to). O has one state and no kicks. Kick tables will be verified by a script that checks the known T-spin-triple setup, not by eye.

nodes.title: Single rAF loop driving gravity, DAS/ARR and lock delay from one dt
nodes.description: Chose rAF with millisecond timers over setInterval. All timing (gravity, horizontal auto-repeat, lock delay) comes from one frame delta, so they can never drift relative to each other and level changes are just a number change. dt is clamped to 100ms so a backgrounded tab does not dump seconds of gravity on return. Rendering happens every frame regardless, which keeps the ghost and lock-delay visuals smooth.

nodes.title: rAF loop with ms accumulator; gravity, DAS/ARR and lock delay share one clock
nodes.description: Chosen over setInterval. Every timed thing (gravity per level, delayed auto shift, auto repeat, lock delay with a move-reset cap) is a millisecond countdown fed by the same frame delta, so pausing is just not calling update(). Level speed uses the guideline curve (0.8 - 0.007*(level-1))^(level-1) seconds per row.

nodes.title: Board is a flat Uint8Array 10 wide x 40 tall, bottom 20 visible
nodes.description: Chosen over row-of-arrays. index = y*10+x. Rows 0..19 are the hidden buffer above the playfield, 20..39 are drawn. Pieces spawn at y=18..19 so the spawn and any kick that lifts a piece never needs a negative-y guard: the bounds check is the same for every cell. Line clear: find full rows, then copyWithin to shift everything above down and zero the top. Game over is 'a locked cell ended in the hidden zone' or 'spawn collides'.

nodes.title: SRS rotation with the standard kick tables from the start
nodes.description: Chosen over runtime matrix rotation. Pieces are stored as four orientations of four [x,y] cells, generated once at load from the spawn shape by rotating within its SRS bounding box (3x3 for JLSTZ, 4x4 for I and O). Kicks are the SRS offset tables: five candidates per rotation transition, tried in order, first non-colliding wins. Doing this in milestone 2 rather than retrofitting in milestone 4 means collision, rotation and kicks are one code path from the beginning. Cost: about 30 lines of tables.

nodes.title: Single rAF loop with dt accumulators for gravity, DAS/ARR, lock delay
nodes.description: Chosen over setInterval. One requestAnimationFrame callback computes dt (clamped to 100ms so a background tab does not dump a second of gravity on return), advances gravity, ticks the held-key repeat timers (DAS 150ms, ARR 40ms so left/right repeat is fast and deterministic across machines), ticks lock delay (500ms, reset on successful shift/rotate, capped by a move counter so infinite stalling is impossible), then renders. Pause is a flag that skips the accumulators but still renders.

nodes.title: M1: index.html + style.css + tetris.js: board renders, piece falls, rAF loop
nodes.description: Three files. tetris.js holds constants (SHAPES as 4 orientations each, COLORS, KICKS), the Uint8Array board, a Game object with spawn/tick/render, and the rAF loop. Milestone 1 ships the loop and gravity with pieces locking on the floor.

nodes.title: M1: index.html + style.css + tetris.js, board renders, piece falls, loop runs
nodes.description: Three files. tetris.js holds the piece table (SRS states), board Uint8Array, a 7-bag randomizer, a rAF loop with gravity, and a canvas renderer. Milestone 1 target: a random piece spawns, falls at level-1 gravity, locks on the floor, next piece spawns.

nodes.title: M1: index.html + style.css + tetris.js: board renders, one piece falls, rAF loop
nodes.description: Three files. tetris.js holds constants (W=10, H=22, HIDDEN=2), SRS piece states, a Uint8Array board, spawn, gravity accumulator, and a draw() that paints settled cells plus the active piece. Lock on floor and spawn the next, so milestone 1 already loops forever rather than stopping after one piece.

nodes.title: M1: index.html + style.css + game.js; board renders, one piece falls, rAF loop
nodes.description: Three files. game.js holds the whole game in a module-pattern closure: constants, piece tables, board, active piece, loop, draw. Milestone 1 scope: canvas sized from board dims, gravity moves the piece down every dropInterval ms, piece locks on the floor and a new one spawns. No input yet.

nodes.title: M1: index.html + canvas renderer + falling piece + rAF loop
nodes.description: Files: index.html, style.css, src/pieces.js (tetromino data, SRS states, kicks, 7-bag), src/board.js (Uint8Array board, collision, lock, clear), src/game.js (state machine + loop), src/render.js (canvas draw), src/input.js (keyboard with DAS/ARR), src/main.js (wiring). Plain script tags in order, no modules, so file:// works in Chrome.

nodes.title: M1: board renders, one piece falls, rAF loop runs
nodes.description: Files: index.html, style.css, js/pieces.js (SRS shapes + kick tables), js/board.js (grid, collision, merge, clear), js/game.js (state + loop), js/render.js (canvas draw), js/input.js, js/main.js. Plain script tags, no ES modules, because file:// blocks module imports in Chrome and the arena rule is 'open index.html and play'.

nodes.title: M1: board renders, one piece falls, rAF loop runs
nodes.description: index.html + style.css + js/{pieces,board,game,render,main}.js as classic scripts (no ES modules, so file:// works in Chrome). Piece shapes as spawn matrices, rotation states precomputed at load. Gravity accumulator in the rAF tick.

nodes.title: M1: board renders, one piece falls, rAF loop runs
nodes.description: Files: index.html, style.css, js/pieces.js (tetromino shapes, colours, SRS states + kicks), js/board.js (grid, collision, merge, clear), js/game.js (state machine, update(dt)), js/render.js (canvas draw), js/input.js (keyboard, DAS), js/main.js (wire-up, loop). Classic scripts, not ES modules, because file:// blocks module imports in Chrome and index.html must open by double-click.

nodes.title: M1: board renders, one piece falls, rAF loop runs
nodes.description: Write index.html, style.css, src/pieces.js, src/board.js, src/game.js, src/render.js, src/input.js, src/main.js. Piece spawns at top, gravity drops it, it locks on the floor and the next spawns. No input yet beyond what falls out of the structure.

nodes.title: M1: index.html + tetris.js with board, falling piece, rAF loop
nodes.description: Write index.html (board canvas, side panel), style.css, tetris.js. tetris.js: PIECES table with SRS orientations, Uint8Array board, spawn, gravity step, lock, render. No input yet beyond what falls out of the structure.

nodes.title: M1 works: commit 72e24b5, pieces fall, lock, stack, top out
nodes.description: Headless run of the engine (DOM stripped, update(16) in a loop) tops out after 7314 frames with 48 filled cells: 12 pieces stacked in the spawn column and then the spawn is blocked. Both spawn rows are tried before declaring game over. No input yet.

nodes.title: M1 works: commit 2b10665, piece falls and locks, loop verified in node harness
nodes.description: Node harness stubs the DOM and runs update(16) for 60 simulated seconds at level 1: three pieces lock (12 cells), matching 1 row/s over 20 rows. Harness lives in the scratchpad, not the repo.

nodes.title: M1 works: commit 9a0107b, SRS states verified by probe, pieces fall/lock/block-out
nodes.description: Headless node probe (DOM stubbed, tetris.js evaluated in a vm) confirmed all 24 generated SRS states equal the reference tables, 12 pieces locked at 800ms/row, and block-out set game over. Generating states by rotating a base matrix beats hand-typing 4 states per piece: one place to be wrong instead of 24.

nodes.title: M1 works: piece falls, locks, stacks, game over on blocked spawn
nodes.description: Commit 3800be7. Verified headless: a scratchpad harness stubs document/canvas/rAF, drives frames with a fixed dt, and prints the board as text. 400 simulated seconds of gravity stack pieces to the top and set over=true. No browser check yet; nothing in the file depends on real canvas behaviour beyond fillRect.

nodes.title: M2: move, rotate with SRS kicks, soft drop, hard drop, lock delay, DAS/ARR
nodes.description: Keyboard input via keydown/keyup into a held-keys set; left/right use DAS 170ms then ARR 40ms so holding a key auto-repeats without relying on OS key repeat. Rotation tries the 5 SRS kicks in order. Lock delay 500ms starts when the piece cannot fall, resets on successful move/rotate up to 15 times, then locks regardless. Hard drop locks instantly. Buffer rows raised from 2 to 4 so an upward kick near the top is never refused by the bounds check (idea from agent-1's 40-row board).

nodes.title: After M1: all ten agents chose canvas + flat/2D board + SRS + rAF
nodes.description: Peeked at 41 decisions across branches. Every agent picked canvas 2D, SRS with kick tables, and a single rAF loop with ms accumulators. Boards split: flat Uint8Array (1,3,5,6,9,10) vs rows-of-arrays (2,4,7,8). Only agent-1 differs in shape: 40 rows with 20 hidden so no cell ever has negative y and kicks that lift a piece need no guard. My collides() already guards y<0 so 22 rows costs nothing. Only agent-3 had committed code; its tetris.js has the guideline gravity curve and a 7-bag, both worth taking at M3. Nothing taken yet.

nodes.title: M2: keyboard input, SRS kicks, DAS/ARR, soft/hard drop, lock delay
nodes.description: Input is a keydown/keyup set plus per-frame polling, not keydown-repeat, so horizontal auto-repeat uses my own DAS (170ms) and ARR (40ms) instead of the OS key repeat. Rotation tries the 5 SRS kicks in order; tables are stored y-up as published and negated at build. Lock delay 500ms with a 15-move reset cap, so a piece cannot be stalled forever on the floor. Hard drop locks immediately. Soft drop is gravity at 20x.

nodes.title: M2: move/rotate/soft/hard drop with SRS kicks, DAS/ARR, 7-bag; split core from DOM
nodes.description: Input goes through a held-keys set read by the loop so DAS (170ms) and ARR (40ms) run on the same clock as gravity. Rotation tries the SRS kick offsets in order and applies the first that fits. Hard drop locks immediately; soft drop is 20x gravity. Pieces come from a 7-bag. The game core takes no DOM references so the whole file loads in node; a mount() at the bottom wires canvas and keyboard only when document exists.

nodes.title: Took 7-bag and the node-loadable module idea from agent-9; changed to a single file with a guarded mount()
nodes.description: agent-9/src/pieces.js has a 7-bag Bag(random) closure with a Fisher-Yates shuffle and an IIFE that exports to module.exports or window so the tables run in node. I took the bag (droughts bounded at 12) and injected the RNG for deterministic tests. Instead of one IIFE per file I keep one file: the game core never touches the DOM, and a mount() at the bottom runs only when document exists, with module.exports set when module exists. Same testability, no file split. Also compared agent-1's 40-row board: my cellAt treats y<0 as air so kicks that lift a piece above row 0 need no special case either.

nodes.title: M1 works: well renders, pieces fall and lock, game over on stack-out
nodes.description: Commit 9d5320c. Verified two ways: node eval of pieces/board/game simulates a no-input game to game over in ~135s virtual time with pieces stacked in the centre column; headless Chrome screenshot shows the well grid and a J piece at spawn. Found and fixed one thing from the screenshot: spawning at board row 0 left the piece invisible in the hidden rows for a full gravity interval, so spawn is now at HIDDEN_ROWS-1. Headless Chrome does not advance rAF under --virtual-time-budget, so the screenshot only proves rendering, not motion; node proves motion.

nodes.title: Read agent-1's 40-row board: removes the y<0 guard, at the cost of 20 buffer rows
nodes.description: agent-1 spawns at y=18 in a 40-tall array so no cell can ever be above the array and the bounds check is uniform. Mine is 22 tall with one 'if (y < 0) continue' in fits(). Not taking it: one line of guard is cheaper to read than a 40-row board with a 20-row offset in every render call. Kept as a data point for the README.

nodes.title: M2: keyboard input with DAS/ARR, SRS kicks, soft/hard drop, lock delay with move-reset cap
nodes.description: Kick tables stored in SRS convention (+y up) and negated on use, so the table can be compared against the wiki by eye. Left/right: instant move, then DAS 170ms, ARR 40ms; last-pressed direction wins. Soft drop is 20x gravity. Hard drop locks at once. Lock delay 500ms, reset by any successful move/rotate up to 15 times, cap refreshed when the piece reaches a new lowest row. Probe will verify an I-piece wall kick and a T-spin-double kick (3->2 test 3) before commit.

nodes.title: M1 works: renders, falls, locks, respawns
nodes.description: Node sim: 120s of ticks at level 1 locks 8 pieces into a valid stack. Headless Chrome screenshot shows settled O and T with an I falling. Gotcha found: headless Chrome fires requestAnimationFrame only once under --virtual-time-budget, so browser checks must call game.tick() synchronously.

nodes.title: M2: move, rotate, soft/hard drop, DAS/ARR, lock delay with move reset
nodes.description: input.js gets a held-key model: keydown moves once and starts a 167ms DAS timer, then 33ms ARR autorepeat, all advanced from the frame loop's dt so it is frame-rate independent. game.js gets move/rotate/softDrop/hardDrop. Lock delay resets on a successful move or rotate while grounded, capped at 15 resets, replenished when the piece reaches a new lowest row (guideline "move reset"). Rotation has no wall kicks yet; that is M4. Also taking DPR canvas scaling and lock-out detection from agent-1.

nodes.title: M2 works: kicks at both walls, lock delay with reset cap, DAS/ARR verified headlessly
nodes.description: T in state 1 at x=-1 rotates cw to state 2 and kicks to x=0. I in state 1 at x=7 rotates to state 2 and kicks to x=6. A piece on the floor locks after 512 ms of updates. A piece wiggled every 100 ms still locks at ~1900 ms because resets cap at 15. Held right on an empty board shifts at frame 11 (176 ms) then every 2.5 frames (40 ms).

nodes.title: Took the tall-hidden-zone idea from agent-1; changed it to 4 buffer rows instead of 20
nodes.description: agent-1's board decision (10x40, bottom 20 visible) exists so kicks and spawns never need a negative-y guard. My fits() already bounds-checks y, so the guard costs nothing, but with only 2 hidden rows an I kick of +2 upward at the top would be refused. Raising BUFFER to 4 covers the largest SRS kick with no other code change and no extra draw work. 20 hidden rows would be equally correct but the extra 160 cells are never used.

nodes.title: M1 works: board renders, pieces fall and lock, rows clear (commit eaff47b)
nodes.description: Verified two ways: (1) Game class run in Node for 60 simulated seconds with a seeded RNG, 3 pieces locked, board dump correct, copyWithin row clear verified on a hand-built board; (2) headless Chrome screenshot shows the field with the I piece at the top. Surprise: the guideline gravity formula is much steeper than remembered (level 10 = 64ms/row, 15 = 7ms), comment fixed to the measured values. Hold/next canvases still at default size.

nodes.title: M3: line clears, scoring, levels, game over, restart
nodes.description: After lock: scan rows bottom-up, copyWithin to drop the rows above each full row. Guideline scoring: 100/300/500/800 x level for 1-4 lines, +1 per soft-drop row, +2 per hard-drop row, back-to-back tetris x1.5. Level = 1 + floor(lines/10), gravity from the guideline curve. Game over shows the overlay; R restarts by rebuilding state. Score/level/lines written to the DOM outputs only when they change.

nodes.title: M1 works: grid + falling piece + loop, verified headless
nodes.description: Headless Chrome (--headless=new --screenshot) shows the grid and a spawned Z with its bottom row at the top visible row. A node harness that stubs document/canvas and calls the exported frame() with synthetic timestamps confirms: y 19 -> 21 after 2s at level 1, 12 filled cells (3 locked pieces) after ~62s, no game over. Gotcha found: Chrome's --virtual-time-budget does not fire requestAnimationFrame, so use --timeout for rAF-driven pages. Exposed window.__tetris debug handle for the harness.

nodes.title: M2: move, rotate with SRS kicks, soft/hard drop, lock delay reset
nodes.description: Game gains move(dx), rotate(dir) that walks the kick table for (from,to), softDrop flag (gravity/20, +1 per row), hardDrop (+2 per row, immediate lock). Lock delay resets on a successful move or rotate while grounded, capped at 15 resets so a piece cannot be stalled forever. input.js maps keydown/keyup to those calls.

nodes.title: Took DPR-scaled canvas backing store from agent-1

Changed: made it the renderer's own sizing step for all three canvases (board, next, hold) instead of a free function, and kept CELL in CSS px so draw code is unchanged.

nodes.title: M1 works: renders, falls, locks, spawns, block-out ends the loop

(1) node probe printed all 28 rotation states from the derived tables and they match SRS exactly; a gravity-only simulation reaches block-out at ~120s with 48 cells stacked. nodes.title: M2: move, rotate with SRS kicks, soft/hard drop, DAS/ARR input
nodes.description: game.js gains move(dx), rotate(dir) that walks the kick table, softDrop(), hardDrop(); lock delay resets on successful move/rotate while grounded, capped at 15 resets per piece, counter cleared when the piece reaches a new lowest row (guideline move-reset). New src/input.js: keydown/keyup tracked in a Set, repeats ignored, DAS 170ms then ARR 30ms accumulated from the same dt as gravity; most recent horizontal press wins. nodes.title: M2 works: 15 probe checks pass incl. T-spin-double kick and I wall kick
nodes.description: Probe built a TSD slot (overhang at (2,19)), placed a T in state 3 beside it, rotated CCW: kick test 3 (-1,-1 in SRS) landed it at (2,19) and hard drop filled rows 20-21. nodes.title: Took generated rotation states from agent-1; verified against my hand tables
nodes.description: agent-1 stores only the spawn shape per piece and derives the other three SRS states by rotating inside the n x n box: (x, y) -> (n-1-y, x), O pinned to its spawn shape. nodes.title: M2: move, rotate with SRS kicks, soft/hard drop, DAS/ARR, lock reset cap
nodes.description: keydown/keyup feed a held-direction stack; the active direction is the top of the stack, first shift is immediate, then DAS 150ms, then ARR 33ms. rotate(dir) walks KICKS[from][dir] and takes the first fit. Soft drop is 20x gravity, hard drop walks down then locks immediately. Lock delay resets on successful shift/rotate while grounded, at most 15 times per piece.

nodes.title: Took 4 hidden rows from agent-3: SRS kicks can lift a piece 2 rows at the ceiling
nodes.description: agent-3 pointed out that several SRS kick offsets move the piece up two rows (dy = -2 in board coordinates). With only 2 hidden rows a piece rotating at the very top can be refused purely by the y < 0 bounds check, which is a rotation the guideline allows. agent-1 solves it with a 40-row board; agent-3 with 4 hidden rows. I went from HIDDEN = 2 to 4, the cheapest fix. The lock-out rule (piece settles entirely in hidden rows = game over) is unchanged.

nodes.title: Took from agent-3: release-resumes-other-direction and spawn-one-row-higher fallback
nodes.description: agent-3/tetris.js onKeyUp: when left is released while right is still held, right restarts its DAS instead of the piece going dead. Also spawn() tries BUFFER-1 then BUFFER-2 before declaring game over, which lets a nearly-full board get one more piece. Took both. Changed: agent-3 tracks input.left, input.right, input.dasDir and input.charged; I replaced left/right/dasDir with a single `held` array (push on keydown, splice on keyup, active dir = last element) so 'newest press wins, release falls back to the older one' is a property of the data structure rather than four branches in two handlers. Noted agent-3 read my graph and chose 4 hidden rows citing my 40-row board; that is a fair simplification and I am keeping 40 because the row count costs nothing with a Uint8Array.

nodes.title: Took DPR canvas scaling from agent-1
nodes.description: agent-1's fitCanvas() sizes the backing store by devicePixelRatio and sets the context transform, so cell bevels are crisp on retina instead of blurred 2x. Mine drew at CSS pixels. Changed: fitCanvas returns the context and the renderer draws in CSS-pixel units W/H instead of reading canvas.width, so no other drawing code had to know about DPR.

nodes.title: M3 works: tetris scores 800, b2b 1200, partial clears keep gap rows, both top-out paths end the game
nodes.description: Headless: 4 rows full except column 9, vertical I hard-dropped -> lines 4, score 834 (800 + 17 rows x 2), board empty. Repeat with b2b -> 1234, level 2 at 13 lines. One full row under a row with a gap clears exactly one and the gap row drops to the bottom. Locking an O entirely in the buffer sets over; a blocked spawn sets over; reset() clears everything.

nodes.title: Took the lock-out rule from agent-1
nodes.description: agent-1's lock() ends the game when every locked cell is in the hidden rows. I only had block-out (spawn collides). Without lock-out a piece can lock invisibly above the well and the player sees nothing settle. Changed: my lock() checks pieceCells before clearLines so the check runs on the piece, not on the board.

nodes.title: M2 works: full movement, drops, DAS, lock delay verified headlessly
nodes.description: Commit bb0e49d. Node checks: T moves 3 left to x=0 and 7 right to x=7 then stops; hard drop locks and spawns next; grounded piece wiggled every 100ms locks at 1900ms (15 resets + 500ms); soft drop covers 4 rows in 200ms at level 1; vertical I in column 9 clears 4 prepared rows. nodes.title: M2 works: 10 node tests pass for walls, kicks, drops, lock delay, DAS
nodes.description: Found and fixed one data bug on the way: the O shape string was 10 chars, so its box size parsed as 3.16 and the O landed one row above the floor. Shape parsing now throws on malformed strings. Tests live in the scratchpad; the game core is require()-able from node because mount() is guarded on document.

nodes.title: M2 works: 22 headless checks pass (I and T wall kicks, DAS/ARR, lock reset cap, drops)
nodes.description: Commit d5212d6. Harness bugs found on the way: feeding one 300ms frame hit the game's 100ms dt clamp, and a zero-length tick dropped the first frame; both were test artefacts, the game was right. Lesson: the harness must step in <=16ms frames like a real browser.

nodes.title: Input: rely on OS keydown auto-repeat for held left/right
nodes.description: Handle every keydown including e.repeat. Zero code, but the repeat delay and rate are whatever the OS is set to (typically 500ms/30ms on macOS), differ per machine, and cannot charge DAS across a piece lock.

nodes.title: Input: held-key model with DAS/ARR on the game clock
nodes.description: Ignore e.repeat. keydown/keyup maintain held state; each frame the input advances a DAS accumulator (delay before auto-shift) then an ARR accumulator (rate between shifts) using the same dt as gravity. Releasing one direction while the other is held resumes the other. DAS charge survives a piece lock.

nodes.title: Took lock-out game over and change-only HUD writes from agent-3; added T-spin scoring on top
nodes.description: agent-3 (commit 6811836) ends the game when a locked piece sits entirely in the hidden rows (lock-out), not just when spawn collides, and writes HUD textContent only when the number changes. Taking both. agent-3 also does back-to-back tetris at 1.5x. I go further: since my probe already proved the 3>2 kick lands a T-spin double, detect T-spins with the 3-corner rule (last action was a rotation, 3 of 4 diagonals around the T centre are solid; full vs mini by the two front corners or kick test 5) and score them per guideline, with B2B covering both tetrises and T-spin clears.

nodes.title: Held-key DAS/ARR input plus lock delay with move-reset AND step-reset
nodes.description: Chose the held-key model (DAS 160ms, ARR 30ms) so left/right feel is the same on every machine and runs off the one game clock. Lock delay is 500ms, reset by a successful move or rotate while grounded, capped at 15 resets per piece so you cannot stall forever. The cap is restored whenever the piece reaches a new lowest row (the Guideline step reset), which agent-3's version lacks: without it, a piece that used its resets high on a ledge and then slides off locks instantly at the bottom, which feels like a bug.

nodes.title: M3: line clears with flash, guideline scoring incl. T-spins and B2B, levels, game over, restart, HUD
nodes.description: Line clear is a two-phase thing: lock finds full rows and enters a 120ms 'clearing' state where those rows flash white, then copyWithin drops the rows above and the next piece spawns. Score: 100/300/500/800 x level; T-spin 400/800/1200/1600, mini 100/200/400; B2B x1.5 on tetris or T-spin lines; soft drop 1/row, hard drop 2/row. Level = 1 + lines/10, gravity from the guideline curve (0.8-0.007(L-1))^(L-1) s. Game over on block-out or lock-out; R restarts by resetting board, bag, and state.

nodes.title: M4: next queue, hold, ghost, T-spin scoring; core split from DOM with guarded mount()
nodes.description: Three-piece next queue fed by the 7-bag. Hold swaps once per piece (C/Shift). Ghost is the piece drawn translucent at its hard-drop row. Wall kicks already exist from M2, so the differentiator is T-spin detection: a T that locks after a rotation with 3 of its 4 diagonal corners filled scores 400/800/1200/1600 x level (mini T-spins not distinguished). Structurally the file is split into a DOM-free core and a mount(document) that runs only in a browser, with module.exports for node, so the headless checks become a real test.js instead of a regex-stripped eval. Canvases are DPR-scaled.

nodes.title: M2: move, rotate with kicks, soft drop, hard drop, lock delay, DAS/ARR
nodes.description: js/input.js: Input class, keydown/keyup to held state, update(dt) drives DAS/ARR. js/game.js: move(), rotate(dir) walking kicksFor(), hardDrop(), soft drop as 20x gravity, grounded() and lock delay with move reset + step reset. js/render.js: DPR-scaled backing store. Keys: arrows, Z/X rotate, Space hard drop, R restart.

nodes.title: Took DPR canvas scaling from agent-1; changed it to one fitCanvas() shared by board, next and hold
nodes.description: agent-1's fitCanvas sets the backing store to css size x devicePixelRatio and applies a setTransform so drawing code stays in CSS pixels. Without it, cell edges blur on retina. I apply the same function to all three canvases and derive the CSS size from COLS/ROWS/CELL rather than the HTML attributes so index.html no longer has to agree with the JS.

nodes.title: M3: guideline scoring, combo, back-to-back, levels, game over overlay, restart
nodes.description: Scoring: 100/300/500/800 x level for 1-4 lines, back-to-back tetris x1.5, combo 50 x count x level, soft drop 1/cell, hard drop 2/cell. Level = 1 + floor(lines/10), which feeds gravityMs. HUD (score/level/lines) lives in the DOM beside the canvas, written only when a value changes. Game over draws an overlay on the canvas; R restarts. Line clear gets a brief flash: cleared rows are held for ~120ms and drawn white before they collapse, so a tetris is visible as an event rather than rows silently vanishing.

nodes.title: Took DAS/ARR held-key model and lock-reset cap from agent-3; DPR scaling from agent-1
nodes.description: From agent-3 (tetris.js, commit 91788da): keydown/keyup feed held state, DAS then ARR accumulators on the frame dt, keyup of one direction resumes the other, lock delay reset on grounded move capped at 15. Changed: added the step reset (cap restored on reaching a new lowest row), moved input into its own Input class that only calls game.move/rotate/hardDrop so game.js stays DOM-free, and made the DAS charge persist through spawn. From agent-1 (decision e2cd955d): scale the canvas backing store by devicePixelRatio so cell edges are crisp on retina. Changed: nothing, it is three lines.

nodes.title: Took the DOM-free core + guarded mount() shape from agent-6 (who took it from agent-9)
nodes.description: My M1-M3 tests worked by regex-stripping everything after the canvas lookup and eval-ing the rest, which is fragile. agent-6 keeps one file with a core that never touches the DOM, exports via module.exports when module exists, and calls mount(document) only when document exists. I adopted that and turned the ad-hoc checks into test.js run with node. Changed: my mount takes the render + input wiring and the core exposes a small API object rather than every internal.

nodes.title: M3: line clears, scoring, levels, gravity curve, 7-bag, lock-out, restart
nodes.description: clearLines scans bottom-up with copyWithin, re-checking the same row after a shift. Score 100/300/500/800 x level, back-to-back tetris 1.5x, +1 per soft row, +2 per hard row. Level = 1 + floor(lines/10); gravity from the guideline curve (0.8 - 0.007*(L-1))^(L-1) seconds. 7-bag randomiser. HIDDEN goes 2 -> 4 and collides() becomes a strict bounds check with no y<0 exemption. Lock-out (all cells locked in hidden rows) and block-out (spawn blocked on both candidate rows) both end the game. R calls reset(), which is also how the game boots. HUD is DOM text, written only when a value changes.

nodes.title: Took gravity curve, 7-bag and scoring table from agent-3; changed the clear scan to re-check in place
nodes.description: agent-3's tetris.js (commit 6811836) has the guideline gravity formula pow(0.8 - (L-1)*0.007, L-1) seconds, a closure-based 7-bag, and 100/300/500/800 with b2b tetris 1.5x. Took all three because they are the published guideline numbers, not taste. Changed: my bag is a state field so reset() can empty it, and my scoring credits soft/hard drop rows at the moment of the drop rather than at lock so a soft-dropped piece that is then moved still scores its rows.

nodes.title: M1 works: board draws, pieces fall and lock, commit e2f4ff0
nodes.description: Verified two ways. Node: 60 simulated seconds at level 1 lock 3 pieces and the gravity curve gives 1000ms/row at level 1, 64ms at level 10. Headless Chrome screenshot of index.html shows the 10x20 grid, HUD and a piece mid-fall. Surprise along the way: pure matrix rotation of the O piece walks it around its 3x3 SRS box, so O's four states are pinned to the spawn state.

nodes.title: Took 4 hidden rows (agent-9, from agent-3) and lock-out (agent-2, from agent-1); dropped my y<0 exemption
nodes.description: My M1/M2 collides() let cells sit at y<0 and lock() silently discarded them, so a piece kicked above the buffer would lose cells with no game over. agent-9 observed that SRS I kicks lift 2 rows, which with HIDDEN=2 and spawn at y=1 reaches y=-1. Two fixes combined: HIDDEN=4 so no legal position ever has y<0, which lets collides() be a strict bounds check (agent-1's argument, without the 40-row board), and the lock-out rule from agent-1: if every locked cell is in a hidden row the game is over.

nodes.title: Took 4 hidden rows from agent-3/agent-9 and lock-out from agent-1; changed: y<0 is now solid so lock() never discards cells
nodes.description: My M2 treated y<0 as open air so ceiling kicks were allowed, but lock() then skipped cells with y<0. That silently loses blocks, the exact plausible-looking fallback the house rules forbid. agent-3 and agent-9 use 4 hidden rows so the SRS dy=-2 kicks stay in bounds; agent-1 ends the game when a piece locks entirely in the hidden rows (lock-out) instead of only on spawn collision (block-out). Took both. Changed: with 4 hidden rows I make y<0 solid like the walls, so the bounds check is uniform and every locked cell lands in the array. Spawn box top moves to row HIDDEN_ROWS-2.

nodes.title: M3: line clears with flash, guideline scoring, levels, block-out and lock-out, restart, HUD
nodes.description: Full rows are found at lock; the game enters a short 'clearing' state (rows drawn white, no piece) then copyWithin collapses them and the next piece spawns. Score: 100/300/500/800 x level, back-to-back tetris 1.5x, +1 per soft-dropped row, +2 per hard-dropped row. Level = 1 + floor(lines/10) feeds gravityMs. Game over on block-out (spawn collides) or lock-out (piece locks entirely in hidden rows). R rebuilds state through newGame(). HUD (score/lines/level) written to the DOM by mount().

nodes.title: M2 works: kicks, drops, lock reset verified in node and headless Chrome
nodes.description: Node tests: T at left wall kicks right by 1; I at right wall kicks left by 1 on R->2; T in a closed pocket refuses rotation; hard drop scores 2/row and spawns next; a piece moved every 400ms on the stack still locks (15-reset cap); soft drop moves 1 row in 50ms at level 1. Headless Chrome at DPR 2 driven by synthetic KeyboardEvents renders the expected stack crisply. Test-writing lesson: two 'failures' were the test's own fault (a bag override before reset, a pocket with no ceiling), the game was right both times.

nodes.title: Held-key input with own DAS/ARR clock; soft drop is a fixed ms/row, not a gravity divisor
nodes.description: Left/right are tracked as held booleans plus a dasDir/dasAcc/charged triple advanced in update(dt): first shift on keydown, then wait DAS 150ms, then one shift every ARR 33ms. Releasing one direction while the other is held resumes the other. Soft drop runs on its own accumulator at min(gravity, 40ms) per row, so at high levels holding down never makes the piece fall SLOWER than gravity would, which is what happens with agent-3's gravity/20 divisor once gravity itself is under 40ms. Rejected: OS key repeat, because the delay and rate differ per machine and cannot be charged during lock.

nodes.title: Lock delay 500ms with move-reset capped at 15 and step-reset on every new lowest row
nodes.description: A grounded piece locks after 500ms. Each successful move or rotate while grounded restarts the timer, up to 15 times per piece. When the piece descends to a row lower than any it has reached before, the reset budget is refilled (Guideline step reset). Without the step reset, a piece that spent its resets on a ledge and then slid off would lock the instant it lands at the bottom. Hard drop locks immediately and ignores all of this.

nodes.title: M2: move, rotate with SRS kicks, soft drop, hard drop, lock delay, held-key input
nodes.description: game.js gains move/rotate/softDrop/hardDrop and the lock-delay state machine; rotate walks the 5 kick offsets from pieces.js. New js/input.js owns keydown/keyup and the DAS/ARR accumulators and is ticked from update(). Spawn now steps down one row if free so the piece appears immediately, and locking with every cell still hidden is a lock-out game over.

nodes.title: Took the held-key DAS/ARR model and release-resumes-other-direction from agent-3
nodes.description: agent-3's tetris.js (commit 91788da) tracks left/right as held flags with dasDir, dasAcc and a charged bit, shifts once on keydown and then repeats on its own clock, and on keyup of one direction resumes the other if still held. Took that shape. Changed: soft drop is its own accumulator with a fixed floor rather than gravity/20, so it cannot be slower than gravity at high levels; DAS/ARR tightened to 150/33.

nodes.title: Took the step-reset for lock delay from agent-8's decision, and spawn-then-step-down and lock-out from agent-8 and agent-3
nodes.description: agent-8 logged (decision 767cce30) that agent-3's 15-reset cap locks a piece instantly at the bottom if the resets were spent on a ledge, and that Guideline step reset fixes it. agent-8's game.js did not have it coded yet when I read it, so this implements the idea from the graph rather than from code: lowestY is tracked per piece and the reset budget refills when the piece goes lower. Also from agent-8: spawn at row 0 then step to row 1 if free so the piece is visible on frame one; from agent-3: locking with no visible cell is a lock-out game over.

nodes.title: Took 4 hidden rows + solid ceiling (agent-3/9/6) and lock-out (agent-1); my merge() was silently dropping cells above row 0
nodes.description: My M1 board let collides() treat y<0 as open air and merge() skipped those cells on lock: a piece kicked above the buffer would lose blocks with no error, exactly the plausible-looking fallback the house rules forbid. agent-3 and agent-9 use 4 hidden rows so the SRS dy=-2 kicks never leave the array; agent-6 additionally makes y<0 solid so bounds checks are uniform; agent-1 ends the game when a piece locks entirely in the hidden rows (lock-out), not only on spawn overlap (block-out). Took all three. Changed: spawn still aims the piece's lowest filled row at the last hidden row, which now leaves exactly 2 rows of kick headroom above every spawn state, and merge() no longer has a y-guard because there is nothing to guard.

nodes.title: Took guideline clear table + b2b tetris 1.5x and change-only HUD writes from agent-3; added a combo counter
nodes.description: agent-3 scores [0,100,300,500,800] x level with back-to-back tetris at 1.5x, and only touches HUD textContent when the value changes. Took both. Changed: consecutive clears also earn a combo bonus of 50 x combo x level (guideline), tracked as a counter that resets on any lock without a clear; b2b state is kept as a boolean but written so T-spins can join it at M4.

nodes.title: M2 works: kicks, drops, lock delay and DAS verified by probe
nodes.description: Node probe over pieces+board+game: I piece rotates off the right wall through its own kick table; lock fires between 400ms and 550ms of rest; continuous grounded moves still lock (reset cap); soft drop steps 3 rows in 3/20 of a gravity interval; 300 random move/rotate/hard-drop steps never leave the active piece overlapping settled cells. Keys: arrows, Z/X, Space, R.

nodes.title: M3: line clears with flash, scoring, levels, game over (block-out + lock-out), restart
nodes.description: lock() stamps the piece, checks lock-out, finds full rows; if any, enters a 'clearing' state for ~180ms with the rows highlighted and no active piece, then removes them, scores (table x level, b2b tetris 1.5x, combo 50 x n x level), bumps level every 10 lines, and spawns. HIDDEN goes to 4 and y<0 becomes solid. R restarts from any state. HUD writes only on change.

nodes.title: M3 works: 22 probe checks pass; probe caught a stale-spin bug before commit
nodes.description: Single/tetris/B2B/TSD scoring, level-up at 10 lines, gravity curve values, lock-out, restart and input-lockout all verified headlessly. The probe found that a T rotated in open air then hard-dropped still scored as a T-spin: the spun flag survived the fall. Fixed by clearing spun in stepDown(). Also learned the clear-flash phase must be drained in tests before placing a new test piece, or spawn() overwrites it.

nodes.title: Took from agent-3: DOM HUD with diffed writes, and the spawn-one-row-higher fallback
nodes.description: agent-3 keeps score/level/lines in DOM elements and only sets textContent when the value changes, with a 'shown' cache. Cleaner than drawing text on canvas and free to style. Also agent-3's spawn() tries HIDDEN-1 then HIDDEN-2 before topping out, which keeps a game alive when the stack touches the first visible row. Changed: I added a fading 'event' line (Tetris +800, B2B Tetris x2 +1250) driven by game.lastClear, which agent-3 does not have, and a combo counter, which agent-3's scoring lacks.

nodes.title: M3 works: scoring, combo, b2b, levels, flash, HUD, game over, restart
nodes.description: Commit 49184b0. Headless: tetris scores 834 incl. hard drop, following b2b tetris 1284 incl. combo; full board spawn sets over; blocked home row falls back to y=0. Screenshot shows the three-column layout with HUD. The flash state means there is a ~120ms window with no active piece; input methods all guard on this.piece so keys during the flash are ignored rather than crashing.

nodes.title: M3 works: tetris 800, b2b 1200, gap rows survive partial clears, lock-out and block-out both end the game, R resets
nodes.description: 21 headless checks. Also confirmed the guideline gravity curve numbers: 1000ms at level 1, 355ms at level 5, 7ms at level 15, under 1ms at 20 (20G). That last one is unplayable by hand but it is the published curve; a cap is a taste decision for M5. Test writing caught two of my own mistakes, not game bugs: I guessed the curve values and I dropped the test I into a column the upper row blocked.

nodes.title: M2 works: walls, kicks, drops, DAS/ARR verified in Node and headless Chrome
nodes.description: Node tests: O stops at both walls; vertical I flush left rotates out via kick; T rotates at the right wall; wiggling piece locks after the 15-reset cap; soft drop moves 4 rows in 200ms at level 1. Bug caught: hardDrop returned 0 because it read the newly spawned piece after locking. Browser: headless Chrome's virtual-time budget does not tick requestAnimationFrame, only timers, so the harness steps the loop from setInterval and dispatches synthetic KeyboardEvents; screenshot shows DAS to both walls and soft drop working.

nodes.title: M3 works: 8 more node tests (clears, tetris scoring, b2b, level-up, lock-out, block-out, ceiling kick), no browser console errors
nodes.description: Line clear test checks a partial row between two full rows slides to the bottom. Tetris in a 4-deep well pays 800 at level 1 and the second in a row pays at least 1200. Lock-out and block-out both end the game. Headless Chrome loads index.html with no console errors.

nodes.title: Scoring: lines-only table times level
nodes.description: 100/300/500/800 x level and nothing else. Simplest, but hides the whole reason SRS kicks exist: a T-spin that scores the same as a normal clear is not worth setting up.

nodes.title: Scoring: full Guideline (T-spin full/mini, back-to-back, combo, perfect clear)
nodes.description: Line table plus T-spin 400/800/1200/1600, mini 100/200/400, both x level; back-to-back 1.5x on consecutive tetris/T-spin clears; combo 50 x n x level; perfect clear 800/1200/1800/2000 x level. Needs the 3-corner rule with kick index for full vs mini, which means the active piece must remember whether its last action was a rotation and which kick landed it.

nodes.title: M4: SRS wall kicks, 4 hidden rows, next queue x5, hold, ghost, T-spin scoring
nodes.description: Kick tables (JLSTZ + I, y-down) indexed by (from,to) rotation state, tried in order; the first offset that fits wins. Hidden rows go from 2 to 4 because the I table's (1,-2) offset lifts the piece two rows and a spawn at row 1 cannot take that. Next shows 5 pieces from the bag queue. Hold swaps once per piece and resets rotation. Ghost is the hard-drop landing drawn as an outline. T-spin uses the 3-corner rule on the last move being a rotation, with mini vs full decided by which corners are filled and whether the last kick was the far (index 4) one.

nodes.title: Guideline scoring with T-spin full/mini, b2b, combo and perfect clear; 4 hidden rows
nodes.description: Chose the full Guideline model. T-spin detection is the 3-corner rule (walls and floor count as filled, above the ceiling does not); full vs mini is 'both front corners filled, or landed on kick test 5'. Perfect clear is the one bonus none of the other nine have, and it costs one every() over the grid after a clear. Also moved from 2 to 4 hidden rows: agent-3 and agent-9 showed that SRS kicks lift a piece up to 2 rows, so with 2 hidden rows a rotation at the ceiling can be refused purely by the bounds check. Spawn is at HIDDEN_ROWS-2 so the piece still emerges on its first step.

nodes.title: M3: line clears, scoring, levels, game over, restart, DOM HUD
nodes.description: game.js: scoreLock() with T-spin kind, b2b, combo, perfect clear; level = 1 + lines/10; active piece tracks spun + kick index. board.js: HIDDEN_ROWS 4, isEmpty(). index.html/style.css: side panel with score, level, lines and a fading clear label; game-over overlay with R to restart. hud.js: change-only textContent writes.

nodes.title: Took 4 hidden rows (agent-3 via agent-9), T-spin kind with kick index (agent-5), combo and change-only HUD writes (agent-4 via agent-3); added perfect clear
nodes.description: agent-9's observation ee1e30ae explains why 2 hidden rows is not enough: kicks with dy=2 at the ceiling get refused by the bounds check. nodes.title: Read agent-7's soft-drop decision: fixed ms/row can be slower than gravity; mine divides gravity so it cannot
nodes.description: agent-7 uses min(gravity, 40ms) per row for soft drop and calls out that a plain gravity/20 divisor is fine but a fixed rate would fall behind gravity at high levels. My soft drop is gravity/20, so holding down is always 20x faster than falling, never slower. Not changing it; noting that the divisor is the safe choice for exactly the reason agent-7 gives.

nodes.title: Ghost: translucent filled copy of the piece (agent-3 style)
nodes.description: Draw the piece at its landing row with alpha ~0.3. Easy, but over a busy stack the translucent fill blends with settled colours and the landing shape is harder to read exactly where it matters.

nodes.title: Ghost: 2px outline in the piece colour, no fill
nodes.description: Stroke each cell inset by 2px in the piece colour. The black interior stays black, so the ghost reads as 'where the edges will be' rather than a faded piece, and it never blends with the stack. Costs 4 strokeRect calls instead of 4 fillRect.

nodes.title: Took T-spin 3-corner detection from agent-5 and combo scoring from agent-2; changed: spin flag lives on the piece and is cleared by any successful non-rotation move, kick index 5 recorded at rotate time
nodes.description: agent-5/tetris.js tspinKind(): T piece, last maneuver was a rotation, at least 3 of the 4 diagonal corners of the 3x3 box are solid; full spin if both corners the T points at are solid or the rotation used kick test 5, else mini. Their commit says a T rotated in the air and then dropped still counted, fixed by clearing the flag on fall. I take the rule and the fix, and clear the flag in tryMove for every successful move, horizontal included, which is what the guideline means by 'last maneuver'. agent-2/src/game.js: combo counter -1 when a lock clears nothing, +1 per consecutive clearing lock, 50 x combo x level. Took as is. Both agents also expose a last-clear label for the HUD; I do the same.

nodes.title: M4 scope: 5-piece preview queue, hold, ghost, T-spins with 3-corner rule, 120ms clear flash
nodes.description: Chosen because these are what separate a toy from a game people keep playing, and all of them fall out of state I already have. Preview needs the bag to feed a queue instead of being popped directly; hold is one field plus a once-per-piece flag; ghost is the hard-drop y computed at draw time; T-spin needs two flags on the piece (last move was a rotation, which kick index succeeded) and a 4-corner probe at lock. The flash makes clears legible at high level and costs one 'clearing' state during which no piece exists. Rejected: 180 rotation and a level cap; neither changes how the game reads.

nodes.title: Outline ghost, 3-deep next queue, hold once per piece, lock-delay pulse on the active piece
nodes.description: Ghost is an outline (see options). Next queue is 3 deep, fed by the 7-bag, matching agent-3's uncommitted M4 because 3 is what modern guideline games show and my preview canvas was already sized for it. Hold is C or Shift, once per piece, reset when a piece locks; the hold panel dims while hold is spent. New on top of what anyone has: while a piece is resting on the stack its cells brighten in proportion to lockAcc/LOCK_DELAY, so the player can see the lock timer running out instead of being surprised by it.

nodes.title: M4: next queue of 5, hold, ghost outline, T-spins, combos, lowest-row lock reset
nodes.description: Bag output goes through a 5-deep queue so the preview shows what the bag will deal. Hold swaps once per piece and resets orientation. Ghost is the piece dropped until it would collide, drawn as an outline so it never reads as a real block. T-spin detection per the 3-corner rule; scoring 400/800/1200/1600, minis 100/200/400, back-to-back applies to tetrises and T-spin clears. Combo 50 x n x level. Lock delay resets count from zero when the piece reaches a new lowest row (guideline), so a piece that falls further gets fresh resets. Wall kicks were already SRS in M2.

nodes.title: M4: next queue (3), hold, outline ghost, lock pulse, preview/hold canvases

nodes.title: Took the 120ms line-clear flash from agent-2; changed row removal to stay allocation-free on the flat array

Changed: agent-2's removeRows filters a row-array board and unshifts new rows; mine walks the full rows top-down and copyWithin's each one so lower indices stay valid, no allocation. nodes.title: M2 works: DAS/ARR timing, I wall kick, T-spin triple entries, hard drop all pass in harness
nodes.description: Node harness drives onKeyDown/onKeyUp with fake events and frame() with 16ms ticks. Verified: immediate shift on press, no repeat before 150ms, repeat to the wall at 33ms, newest direction wins, release resumes the older one. I vertical at the left wall rotates via kick. T-spin triple: built the classic slot and searched every resting T position; found exactly 'state 0 at (1,35) cw -> R at (0,37)' and 'state 2 at (0,35) ccw -> R at (0,37)', the two textbook entries. nodes.title: M3: scoring (T-spin, B2B, combo, perfect clear), levels, game over, restart, HUD
