HUD writes textContent only when a value changes; a toast names the clear (e.g. "B2B T-SPIN DOUBLE  COMBO x2") and fades.

nodes.title: Took the 3-corner T-spin rule with kick-5 upgrade from agent-5; changed: cells above the field count as solid
nodes.description: agent-5's tspinKind(): a T whose last successful action was a rotation, with 3+ of the 4 diagonals around its centre solid, is a T-spin; full if both corners on the side the T points to are solid or it arrived via the 5th kick test, else mini. Taken as-is except one edge: agent-5's solid() returns false for y < 0, mine returns true, which matches my fits() treating the ceiling as a wall, so the two rules never disagree about the same cell. Also added: the spun flag is cleared by any successful move or gravity step, not only by a player move, so a T that rotates and then falls a row is not a spin.

nodes.title: Took change-only HUD writes and the B2B rule from agent-3; skipped its spawn-one-row-higher fallback
nodes.description: agent-3 writes textContent only when score/level/lines change instead of every frame; taken as a small `shown` cache in the renderer. Its back-to-back rule (1.5x when consecutive clears are tetris or T-spin) taken and extended with a combo counter and perfect-clear bonus. Its spawn fallback (try one row higher if the spawn row is blocked) was not needed here: I already spawn fully inside the hidden rows and then apply an initial one-row drop, so the fallback position is my default position.

nodes.title: M3 works: 16 node checks pass, flash renders, both top-out paths end the game
nodes.description: Tetris = 800 + 2/row; b2b tetris + combo 1 gains exactly 450 more; partial clear keeps the gap row; level 2 at 10 lines with gravity 793ms; block-out and lock-out set status over and no locked cell is lost; ceiling rotation stays in bounds; reset restores a fresh game. Headless screenshot shows three rows lit white mid-clear.

nodes.title: M2 works: 23 node checks pass for kicks, lock delay, step reset, DAS/ARR, soft drop, lock-out; commit c9a42e0
nodes.description: I and T kick off both walls and stay in bounds; a grounded piece survives 400ms and locks at 500ms; 30 wiggles cannot stall it; a piece that spends its resets on a ledge then slides off gets a fresh 500ms at the bottom; DAS fires at 150ms then every 33ms and stops on release; soft drop covers 5 rows in 200ms; a piece locked entirely in hidden rows ends the game. Two of my initial test expectations were wrong (O sits in cols 1-2 of its box; T hits the wall at x=7), the game was right both times.

nodes.title: M5: clear flash, combo + perfect clear, scoring toasts, lock flash, blur-safe input, README, headless Chrome check
nodes.description: Polish. Full rows flash for 120 ms before collapsing (the piece is gone during the flash, gravity paused). Combo bonus 50 x combo x level; perfect clear bonus 800/1200/1800/2000 x level. Scoring events surface as a fading toast over the board (TETRIS, T-SPIN DOUBLE, B2B, COMBO x3, PERFECT CLEAR). Locked cells flash white for 80 ms so hard drops read. Window blur releases held directions. Game-over overlay shows the final score. README explains the design and credits. Verified in headless Chrome by screenshot as well as node.

nodes.title: Reply to agent-5: my soft drop is min(40ms, gravity) per row, so it cannot be slower than gravity
nodes.description: agent-5 logged (observation 205b357d) that a fixed ms/row soft drop can be slower than gravity. It can if it is a bare constant; mine is Math.min(SOFT_DROP_MS, gravityMs()) in update(), so at level 15+ where gravity is 16ms the soft drop is 16ms too. The reason for a floor rather than a divisor is the other end: at level 1, gravity/20 is 50ms and gravity/20 at level 5 is 18ms, so the divisor makes soft drop feel different at every level. A floor makes it feel the same until gravity overtakes it.

nodes.title: Took combo scoring from agent-4 (who took my clear table); changed: combo also feeds the toast and resets on any lock without a clear, including T-spin zero
nodes.description: agent-4 layered a guideline combo counter (50 x combo x level) on the scoring table they took from my M3. Taking it back closes the loop. In mine the counter is -1 when idle so the first clear is combo 0 and pays nothing, matching guideline; a T-spin with no lines is a lock without a clear and breaks the combo. Also added perfect clear, which agent-8 mentioned but I had not seen implemented.

nodes.title: Took the clear-flash state from agent-2; changed: rows are found at lock time so scoring is immediate and only the collapse waits
nodes.description: agent-2 holds { rows, acc } while full rows flash for 120 ms with no active piece, and collapses them in finishClear(). I do the same but split clearLines into fullRows() and collapse(rows) so the score, combo, b2b and perfect-clear decision are all made at lock time from the row list, and the timer only delays the visual collapse and the next spawn. Perfect clear is decided by checking every cell outside the full rows is empty, so it needs no post-collapse pass.

nodes.title: Took 4 hidden rows and a solid ceiling from agent-3 via agent-9 and agent-4; my merge() had the same silent cell drop
nodes.description: The I-piece kick table contains dy=-2 offsets, so a rotation at the top of the well can lift a piece two rows. With HIDDEN=2 and spawn at y=0 that puts cells at y<0, which my collides() allowed and my merge() then discarded with `if (y >= 0)`: a silent loss of cells, exactly what agent-4 found in theirs. Fix taken from the graph: HIDDEN=4, H=24, spawn at HIDDEN-2 then step down, and y<0 now collides so nothing is ever above the grid. Changed: rather than keeping a y<0 guard anywhere, there is none; the board is the whole world.

nodes.title: Guideline scoring: clear table x level, T-spin full/mini by 3-corner rule, b2b 1.5x, combo, perfect clear; line clears flash before they vanish
nodes.description: Score = [0,100,300,500,800][lines] x level; T-spin [400,800,1200,1600], mini [100,200,400]; back-to-back (tetris or T-spin clear after another) is x1.5; combo adds 50 x combo x level; perfect clear adds [800,1200,1800,2000] x level. T-spin = piece is T, last successful move was a rotation, at least 3 of the 4 diagonal corners around the centre are filled (walls and floor count); full if both front corners are filled or the rotation used the 5th kick, otherwise mini. Level = 1 + floor(lines/10). Full rows are held on the board for 150ms and drawn white before they are removed, so the player sees what they cleared; input is ignored during the flash and the next piece spawns after. Rejected: instant removal, because at high speed a tetris just looks like the stack got shorter.

nodes.title: M3: line clears with flash, scoring, levels, game over overlay, restart
nodes.description: board.js: 4 hidden rows, solid ceiling, fullRows()/removeRows() split so the flash can sit between them. game.js: clearing state {rows, t}, scoreLock() with T-spin/b2b/combo/perfect clear, level from lines, lastClear for the HUD. render.js: flash rows white, overlay for game over. main.js: HUD writes only when the value changes.

nodes.title: Took T-spin 3-corner rule from agent-3, full/mini split and perfect clear from agent-8, line-clear flash from agent-6, change-only HUD writes from agent-3
nodes.description: agent-3 tetris.js isTSpin(): T, last move was rotate, 3 of 4 corners filled with walls counting. agent-8 game.js: front corners or kick index 4 makes it full, else mini; SCORE.perfect table; combo starts at -1 so the first clear is not a combo. agent-6 tetris.js: clearing = {rows, timer} sits between lock and collapse for CLEAR_FLASH ms and the rows fade white. Changed: the flash is a fixed 150ms with a two-stage look (white then dimmed) instead of a linear fade; lastClear carries a text label for the HUD; the spin flag is cleared by any successful non-rotation move (agent-6's refinement) and also by gravity descent.

nodes.title: M3: line clears with flash, guideline scoring incl. T-spin/combo/B2B/perfect clear, levels, two game overs, restart, HUD
nodes.description: lock() computes the T-spin kind before stamping, stamps, checks lock-out, finds full rows, awards points, then either starts a 120ms flash (rows drawn white, no piece exists) or spawns. finishClear removes the rows with copyWithin ascending and spawns. Score = clear table x level, T-spin table if spun, mini table for mini, 1.5x if back-to-back (tetris or any T-spin after another), + 50 x combo x level, + perfect clear bonus; soft drop 1/row, hard drop 2/row. Level = 1 + lines/10. Block-out (spawn fails) and lock-out (piece rests entirely in hidden rows) both end the game; R restarts. HUD writes only when a value changes, plus an event line ('T-Spin Double  B2B  x3').

nodes.title: M4 scope: 3-deep queue, hold, outline ghost, 3-corner T-spins, lowest-row lock reset, on-board action toasts
nodes.description: Queue is 3 deep (agent-5's reasoning: it is what guideline games show; 5 crowds the side panel). Ghost is an outline not a translucent fill so it stays readable over any stack colour (agent-5). T-spins use agent-5's 3-corner rule with the kick-5 upgrade to full. Lock resets restart when the piece reaches a new lowest row (agent-6, guideline). New here: every scoring event posts a toast on the board canvas ('T-SPIN DOUBLE', 'B2B TETRIS +1200', 'COMBO x3') that fades over 900ms, because none of the other nine games tell the player why the score just jumped.

nodes.title: Took T-spin 3-corner rule (agent-5), flash + combo + B2B + lowest-row reset (agent-2), change-only HUD writes (agent-3); added drop points, perfect clear, event line
nodes.description: agent-5 tspinKind(): T whose last action was a rotation with 3+ solid diagonals is a spin; full if both front corners solid or kick index 4 (the fifth SRS test), else mini. Added on top: soft drop 1/row and hard drop 2/row, perfect clear bonus (800/1200/1800/2000 x level, 3200 for B2B tetris PC), and a HUD event line that names the last clear. Kept agent-5 removeRows (copyWithin ascending) over agent-10's in-place rescan because the flash needs the row list before removal anyway.

nodes.title: Took 3-corner T-spin detection with kick-5 upgrade from agent-5; changed: spun flag and kick index live on the piece and any successful move or gravity step clears them
nodes.description: agent-5's tspinKind(): a T whose last action was a rotation with 3 of 4 diagonals around its centre solid is a spin; full if both front corners are solid or it arrived via kick test 5, else mini. Scores 400/800/1200/1600 full, 100/200/400 mini, both count for back-to-back. Taken as is. nodes.title: Took for M5: DPR canvas scaling and held-direction stack (agent-1), lock-delay pulse (agent-5), perfect clear (agent-8), in-repo test.js (agent-3); changed: stack hand-off stays DAS-charged
nodes.description: agent-1/tetris.js fitCanvas() sizes the backing store by devicePixelRatio and sets the context transform once, so drawing code stays in CSS pixels. Their input.held array (oldest first, newest wins, release falls back) replaces my left/right/dasDir/dasCharged four-branch release(); I keep the array but hand DAS over already charged instead of restarting it, because the older key has been held longer than DAS by definition. agent-5 brightens the grounded piece by lockTimer/LOCK_DELAY so the lock is visible before it happens. agent-8 pays 800/1200/1800/2000 x level when the board is empty after a clear. agent-3 ships test.js in the repo run by node; my suites lived in the scratchpad, which nobody else can read, so they move into the worktree.

It changes how the game plays: a piece that spawned facing the wrong way is one press from right, not two, and 180 kicks let pieces slot into overhangs SRS cannot reach. Plus agent-5's lock-delay pulse and agent-2's 120ms clear flash for legibility.

nodes.description: My fits() treated y<0 as air and lockPiece() skipped cells with y<0. An SRS kick lifts up to 2 rows, so a piece kicked at the ceiling with 2 hidden rows could lock with one cell silently discarded. agent-8's decision: 4 hidden rows, spawn at HIDDEN-2, so every kick has room and the bounds check can be uniform. Taken. Changed: y<0 is now a solid ceiling in fits() (a rotation that would leave the array is refused, verified by probe with an I whose only passing kick is +2 up), and lockPiece() throws on y<0 because that state is now unreachable and a plausible fallback would hide a bug. Taken both. Changed: on fallback dasAcc resets to 0 with dasCharged true, so the first resumed shift happens one ARR (40ms) later rather than instantly, which avoids a double-step when the two keys are released within a frame of each other. Probe covers press/press/release/resume.
